vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: arista-device-health
Version: 0.1.0

The skill bundle provides a legitimate and well-structured procedure for diagnosing Arista EOS device health. It utilizes standard EOS commands and Linux-native diagnostic tools (e.g., `bash top`, `bash free`, `bash dmesg`) as intended for the platform, with no evidence of data exfiltration, unauthorized access, or malicious intent in SKILL.md or _meta.json.

llm.summary: The skill is an instruction-only, read-only triage checklist for Arista EOS devices and its requested actions and artifacts are consistent with that purpose.

dimensions.detail: Name and description match the instructions: the SKILL.md contains step-by-step, device-focused commands (show, show agent, show interfaces, optional bash diagnostics) appropriate for Arista EOS troubleshooting. There are no unrelated credentials, binaries, or install steps required.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: Instructions are narrowly scoped to on-device diagnostics (show commands, agent logs, interface and environment checks). They do reference running Linux-native commands via 'bash' (top, free, dmesg) and reading agent logs — this is expected for EOS but means the operator/agent will see potentially sensitive device state (logs, configs). The procedure does not direct data to external endpoints or request unrelated system files.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No install spec or code files — instruction-only skill. This minimizes disk-write and supply-chain risk.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill declares no environment variables, credentials, or config paths. It does require out-of-band SSH/console access as a prerequisite (normal for a network troubleshooting run). There are no disproportionate secret or credential requests embedded in the instructions.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: always is false and the skill is user-invokable; it does not request persistent installation or modify other skills or system-wide agent settings. Autonomous invocation is allowed (platform default) but the skill itself contains only read-only diagnostic steps.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This is an instruction-only, read-only Arista troubleshooting checklist and appears coherent with its stated purpose. Before running it: ensure you have authorized SSH/console access (privilege level), run non-destructive/read-only commands first, and avoid applying any remediation steps you don't fully understand. Because the skill source and homepage are unknown, prefer testing the procedure on a non-production device or a maintenance window and avoid copying sensitive logs or configs to untrusted external services. If you need automation, verify any tooling that executes these commands is from a trusted source and follows your change-control policies.
